sentence: This project studies how tumors start, grow, spread and resist therapy by looking at cancer through the ideas of evolution and mathematical models.
This project builds a tool that releases tiny doses of many drugs inside a patient's tumor to find out which drugs work for that patient.
This project builds an imaging method using sodium and proton signals to find out early whether breast cancer is responding to chemotherapy.
This project tests whether an approved drug that activates a receptor can help kidneys recover in chronic kidney disease, using mouse models.
This project tests whether immune checkpoint blockade therapy is safe and helps against chronic bone and joint infections in mice.
This project studies how breathing menthol, mint and tobacco flavored e-cigarette vapor affects the lungs, including lungs that already have disease.
This project studies what ribosomes do in gut cells that change form after injury, and how this relates to tissue regrowth and cancer.
This project builds custom equipment that connects research tools to experimental samples and shares device designs to help vision research.
This project studies how alcohol and acetate change the way astrocytes read their genes, and how this may relate to alcohol use disorder.
This project builds a device that automates the comet assay so DNA damage in cells can be measured simply and quickly.
This project studies how methamphetamine use leads to thinking problems in people with HIV, using brain scans and machine learning.
This project tests whether molecular tests for leftover leukemia cells can predict which children with acute myeloid leukemia will relapse.
This project reads viral DNA and RNA from stool, urine, blood, mouth, nose and skin samples to describe the viruses living in people.
This project builds a screening platform that tests many designs of chimeric antigen receptors to find which ones work best for T cell therapy.
This project tests whether too much inflammation upsets the balance between the host and its bacteria and so causes periodontitis.
This project uses brain scans, including MRI, to follow a group of people over time and study early signs of synucleinopathy.
This project studies how senescent cells and immune cells communicate in uterine fibroids to cause fibrosis.
This project studies how viral proteins pack DNA into empty protein shells, and which structural features affect this process.
This project builds a one-time gene therapy that lowers the prion protein to treat, prevent or delay prion disease, and tests it in mice.
This project studies how a gene that regulates interneurons changes their development in neurodevelopmental disorders.
